Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Pinnacle Global Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions are to register any questions via the Q&A tool now. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Pinnacle Global Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are David Hargrove, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Hargrove.

David Hargrove: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust assets under management growth, record client inflows, and the appeal of our diversified product offerings across equities, fixed income, and alternatives.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. From a financial perspective, Pinnacle Global Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $2.1 billion, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, elevated fee rates in our alternatives and active strategies, and robust net client inflows. Our expenses were $1.45 billion, resulting in net income of $480 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in key growth initiatives.

As we dive deeper into our financial results, I'd like to start with our core franchise metric: assets under management, or AUM. I'm pleased to report that we delivered another quarter of robust AUM growth, reflecting strong market tailwinds, record client inflows, and the continued appeal of our differentiated product suite.

Let me walk you through the headline numbers first. Ending AUM reached a record $1.28 trillion as of September 30th, up 4.8% quarter-over-quarter from $1.22 trillion at the end of Q2, and up 13.2% year-over-year from $1.13 trillion in Q3 2023. This performance marks our eighth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outpacing the industry average of 2-3% QoQ as reported by Morningstar data.

Breaking it down, our AUM expansion was driven by a combination of factors: market appreciation contributed $38 billion, or about 65% of the QoQ increase; net client inflows added a stellar $18 billion – our highest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021; and foreign exchange and other tailwinds chipped in the remainder. On a YoY basis, market gains accounted for roughly 55% of growth, with inflows representing 35%. Notably, our annualized organic growth rate – net inflows divided by average AUM – stood at 5.8%, well ahead of peers like T. Rowe Price and State Street Global Advisors.

Now, turning to the breakdown by asset class, which underscores the diversification and resilience of our platform. Equities represent 47% of total AUM at $602 billion, with QoQ growth of 6.2%, YoY growth of 16.8%, and net inflows of $9.5 billion. Fixed income is 27% at $346 billion, up 2.1% QoQ and 9.4% YoY, with $4.2 billion in net inflows. Alternatives make up 17% at $218 billion, surging 8.4% QoQ and 22.7% YoY, with $6.1 billion in net inflows. Multi-asset and cash equivalents are 9% at $115 billion, up 1.9% QoQ and 7.2% YoY, with net inflows of $1.7 billion after minor outflows of $0.5 billion. Total AUM hits 100% at $1,281 billion, with the 4.8% QoQ and 13.2% YoY growth, and $18 billion in net inflows.

Equities, our largest segment at $602 billion, benefited from broad-based rallies across global indices. US large-cap strategies, particularly our active growth equity funds mirroring the S&P 500's 5.1% QoQ return, drove that +6.2% growth. We saw $9.5 billion in net inflows here, fueled by retail demand for our low-cost ETFs like the Pinnacle S&P 500 ESG Enhanced ETF, which has gathered $4 billion in AUM since its January launch. Emerging markets equities, however, lagged with flat flows amid China slowdown concerns, though our India-focused small-cap fund outperformed the MSCI India Index by 450 basis points.

In fixed income, AUM grew to $346 billion amid falling Treasury yields – the 10-year note dropped 25 basis points QoQ to 3.75%. Duration extension in our core-plus strategies positioned us well, with +2.1% growth and $4.2 billion inflows. Institutional clients favored our short-duration and municipal bond ladders, especially post-Fed's September rate cut. That said, we experienced modest outflows from legacy high-yield funds as spreads tightened to 320 basis points over Treasuries, prompting us to pivot toward opportunistic credit via our new CLO ETF.

Alternatives continues to be our fastest-growing powerhouse, surging 8.4% QoQ to $218 billion – now 17% of total AUM, up from 14% a year ago. Net inflows of $6.1 billion were propelled by private markets demand: our evergreen private equity interval fund raised $2.8 billion from high-net-worth individuals seeking yield amid equity volatility, while hedge fund-of-funds strategies returned 7.2% net QoQ, beating the HFRI Fund Weighted Composite by 210 basis points. We've also scaled our direct lending platform through a strategic JV with Ares Management, targeting middle-market loans with 9-11% yields.

Multi-asset and cash equivalents rounded out at $115 billion, with steady but lower growth as clients rotated into higher-beta assets.

Regionally, the Americas remain our bedrock at 62% of AUM, $795 billion, up 5.2% QoQ on strong US institutional mandates. EMEA grew 3.9% to 24%, $307 billion, driven by UK DC pension inflows into our sustainable fixed income mandates under SFDR Article 8/9 classifications. Asia-Pacific was the star, expanding 7.1% to 14%, $179 billion, with $3.2 billion inflows from sovereign wealth funds in Singapore and Australia favoring our quant-alternatives suite – our APAC AUM has doubled since 2022.

From a strategic lens, this AUM trajectory validates our 'Diversified Alpha 3.0' initiative: we've deployed AI-driven portfolio construction tools across 70% of our equity and alternatives strategies, enhancing alpha generation – our active equities beat benchmarks by 120 basis points on average over three years. We're also accelerating ETF conversions, with five new UCITS-compliant products launching in Q4 to capture €20 billion in European flows. Amid geopolitical risks and persistent inflation, clients are de-risking via alternatives, now 25% of institutional allocations versus 18% industry average per Preqin, and our 60/40 hybrid multi-asset solutions are resonating.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 AUM growth of 3-5% QoQ, assuming stable markets, with alternatives and ETFs as key drivers.

I'd now like to turn to our compensation ratio, which we define as total compensation and benefits expense as a percentage of revenue – a key metric in our industry that reflects our discipline in managing one of our largest operating costs while attracting and retaining top talent in a highly competitive talent market.

For the quarter, our compensation ratio came in at 47.2%, a 110 basis point improvement sequentially from 48.3% in Q2 and down 240 basis points year-over-year from 49.6% in Q3 2023. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement and underscores the leverage we're generating from our revenue growth outpacing compensation expense growth. On a trailing twelve-month basis, the ratio was 48.5%, down from 51.2% in 2023 and materially better than the 54.1% we reported in 2022 amid the post-pandemic hiring surge. For context, this figure is at the lower end of our peers – think BlackRock's reported 46-48% range or T. Rowe Price's mid-40s – and well below the 55%+ averages seen in pure-play hedge funds like Citadel or Millennium, where performance fees drive outsized variable pay.

Total compensation expense for Q3 was $990 million, up 4% year-over-year but flat sequentially, representing about 72% of our non-interest operating expenses. Revenue, meanwhile, grew 11% YoY, fueled by a 12% increase in average AUM to $1.25 trillion, higher fee rates in our alternatives and active equity strategies, and robust net inflows of $18 billion, including strong flows into our suite of low-cost ETFs like the Pinnacle S&P 500 ESG Tracker, which now manages over $50 billion.

The YoY comp growth was moderated by several factors. Base salaries, which comprise roughly 45% of our total comp mix, rose only 2.5% overall, reflecting targeted merit increases of 3-4% for our 2,800-strong global workforce, with a focus on retaining portfolio managers and quants in high-demand areas like multi-asset and private markets. Variable compensation – bonuses and incentives – made up 35% of the total and increased 7% YoY, but as a percentage of revenue, it declined due to our outperformance against benchmarks. For instance, our core active equity strategies beat their Lipper peers by 150 basis points net of fees, triggering performance hurdles that aligned payouts with client alpha generation.

Equity-based compensation, at 20% of the mix, was up modestly due to higher grant values tied to our TSR performance – we delivered strong total shareholder return this year. However, we're amortizing these over longer vesting periods, with 60% now subject to four-year cliffs versus three years previously, which helps smooth expense recognition and ties retention to long-term value creation.

Regionally, we saw some variance that influenced the ratio. In the Americas, which account for 65% of our AUM and 70% of headcount, the comp ratio was 49%, pressured by the U.S. talent wars – we've added 120 specialists in quant trading and ESG integration since Q1, competing with the likes of Renaissance Technologies and Vanguard's ETF expansion. Salaries here average 15% above European peers, but our deferred comp structure – 40% of bonuses deferred into Pinnacle stock with clawback provisions – has kept turnover below 8%, versus industry averages north of 12% per Heidrick & Struggles data.

In EMEA, the ratio improved to 45%, benefiting from more stable hiring markets and our focus on London and Frankfurt hubs. Revenue growth from UCITS-compliant active ETFs and model portfolios for wealth platforms like UBS and Schroders drove top-line expansion outpacing a flat comp base. APAC was our star performer at 43%, with inflows into our Asia ex-Japan equity and China+ strategies. Here, we've leveraged lower local talent costs – Singapore-based PMs earn 20-25% less than New York counterparts – while investing in Mandarin-speaking distribution teams to capture the emerging wealth transfer.

Strategically, we're driving further ratio compression through technology and automation initiatives. We've deployed significant resources into AI-driven portfolio optimization and risk platforms, partnering for custom quant models that have reduced manual oversight in our systematic strategies. This has allowed us to flatten headcount growth versus industry-wide trends. Early pilots in robotic process automation for trade reconciliation are targeting additional efficiency gains in back-office comp.

Second, compensation redesign for performance alignment: a larger portion of variable pay for investment professionals is tied to three-year AUM retention and organic net flows, with malus adjustments for underperformance and expanded ESG-linked incentives vesting based on net-zero milestones.

Third, scale through product innovation. Our ratio benefits from the high-margin profile of ETFs and alternatives: ETFs contribute significantly at low average fees, delivering operating leverage. Launches like crypto-related products are zero-headcount revenue drivers. In alternatives, our private credit platform grew strongly, with carry fees at minimal incremental comp cost.

Looking forward, we expect the comp ratio to trend toward 46-47% on a full-year basis, assuming continued AUM growth and inflows.

Let me also touch on our efficiency ratios, with a particular focus on our expense ratio – a key metric that underscores our operational discipline and competitive edge. Our weighted average expense ratio stood at 38 basis points for the quarter, down 12% year-over-year from 43 basis points, and marking continued improvement.

The expense ratio is calculated as total operating expenses – excluding variable distribution costs like 12b-1 fees – divided by our average monthly AUM. At around $1.25 trillion in average AUM, this reflects the power of our scale. For comparison, the Morningstar average is around 62 basis points, with peers like BlackRock at 41 basis points and Vanguard at low single digits on index products. Our blended ratio benefits from low-cost ETFs and index strategies, now over half of AUM.

Administrative and general expenses fell, driven by AI-powered reconciliation tools reducing errors and cycle times, building on cloud-based data management for our ETF platform, including flagships like the Pinnacle S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF and active semi-transparent ETFs. Investment advisory fees held steady amid pricing pressure, while marketing costs dropped via digital channels lowering cost per new account.

This quarter's improvement continues a multi-year trajectory, compressing significantly since 2020 and outpacing peers. It held despite shifts in active strategies, offset by ETF inflows into thematic products.

Regionally, Americas at 32 basis points benefiting from regulatory tailwinds like T+1 settlement. Europe improved via UCITS efficiencies. APAC higher but clawing back through fintech partnerships for robo-advisory.

Strategically, targeting sub-35 basis points through product innovation like new active ETFs, tech modernization with gen AI for surveillance, and selective M&A blending high-margin private assets with scale.

Our broader efficiency shines: operating margin expanded reflecting disciplined expense growth against revenue gains.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging AI tools and active conviction positioning.

As Chief Investment Officer, I'm pleased to dive into our fund performance relative to peers and benchmarks for the quarter ended September 30th. Overall, our strategies continue to demonstrate resilient alpha generation amid a volatile macro environment marked by persistent inflation pressures, Fed rate hike uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions. Across the relevant portions of our platform – up 8% quarter-over-quarter – we delivered risk-adjusted returns that outperformed 72% of our peer group on a Morningstar basis, with an average information ratio of 0.45 across core strategies.

Let me break this down by asset class, starting with equities, our largest exposure. Our flagship Pinnacle Global Equity Fund returned 5.2% gross of fees for the quarter, net outperforming its MSCI ACWI benchmark by 180 basis points. Year-to-date, we're up 14.7% versus the benchmark's 11.9%, ranking in the top decile of the Lipper Global Large-Cap Growth peer universe, which averaged 12.1% YTD. This outperformance was driven by our overweight in US technology and healthcare – sectors where stock selection added 120 bps of alpha. For instance, conviction overweights in mega-caps like NVIDIA and Eli Lilly contributed 75 bps, capitalizing on AI and drug tailwinds, while we navigated cyclicals by trimming energy early.

Regionally, US large-cap strategies shone, with the Pinnacle S&P 500 Enhanced Index Fund delivering 6.1% – 150 bps ahead of the S&P 500's 4.6% – thanks to smart beta incorporating quality and momentum, beating Vanguard by 90 bps and first quartile peers. European equities returned 3.8% versus STOXX 600's 4.2%, mitigated by active FX hedging covering 40% of exposures. Emerging markets: 2.9% trailing MSCI EM slightly on China issues, but outperformed 65% of peers by pivoting to India staples.

Shifting to fixed income, strategies generated 2.8% returns, ahead of Bloomberg US Aggregate's 1.9% by 90 bps. Pinnacle Core Bond ranked top quintile versus peers, with duration at 5.8 years and overweight in BBB corporates adding value. Barbell approach yielded superior Sharpe to BlackRock's ETF. Regionally, UK gilts lagged but Aussie/NZ bonds provided ballast.

In alternatives, our platform posted strong results, with multi-strategy hedge up 4.5% net, outpacing HFRI by 170 bps. Private credit at 7.2% annualized topping peers via middle-market lending. Real assets benefited from renewables.

We've enhanced performance through AI optimization across most strategies, improving factor timing and cutting trading costs. ESG mandates outperformed by 40 bps.

Strategically, overweight quality growth in US, selective EM, defensive fixed income with TIPS. Risk controls robust, targeting organic growth via performance fees.

In summary, our benchmark-agnostic approach delivers superior returns versus peers like Vanguard, BlackRock, and Fidelity.

David Hargrove: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes sustained AUM growth of 3-5% in Q4, further comp ratio compression to 46-47%, ongoing fund outperformance, and expense ratio targeting sub-35 bps through innovation and scale.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Larson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Larson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind the strong AUM inflows, particularly in alternatives?

David Hargrove: Good morning, Mike. Happy to address that. As Lisa detailed, the $18 billion in net inflows were broad-based, but alternatives led with $6.1 billion, driven by our evergreen private equity interval fund raising $2.8 billion from high-net-worth clients seeking yield, and hedge fund-of-funds beating benchmarks. The JV with Ares for direct lending also resonated amid yield hunts. This aligns with clients allocating more to alts – 25% versus industry 18% – and we see this continuing.

Mike Larson: Thank you. And a follow-up on your outlook for the compensation ratio – how sustainable is the improvement?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Mike. The 47.2% Q3 ratio reflects revenue leverage from 11% growth outpacing comp expenses. Sustainability comes from our three pillars: tech automation flattening headcount, pay redesign tying more to long-term flows and ESG, and high-margin products like ETFs and private credit. We guide to 46-47% full-year, barring major hiring surges, with deferrals and malus keeping alignment tight.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jennifer Hale with Morgan Stanley.

Jennifer Hale: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Pinnacle Global Equity Fund?

Robert Kline: Good morning, Jennifer. Absolutely. The fund returned 5.2% net for Q3, beating MSCI ACWI by 180 bps and ranking top decile YTD in Lipper peers. Key was stock selection in tech and healthcare adding 120 bps, with NVIDIA and Eli Lilly overweights shining on AI and GLP-1 trends. Our smart beta and AI tools enhanced this, and we're positioned for dispersion with quality growth focus.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Hargrove for closing remarks.

David Hargrove: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Pinnacle Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
